analyst_test: The careful but hurried pass is the union of the six recorded Fryele runs' methods: it cleans and crosswalks every file, reconstructs each block's diesel use tank to tank for the fuel-cost ask, fits the pilot's battery energy per bus-day on kilometres, hours, climb, timetable speed and a nonlinear temperature term with a block effect, reads the first-winter capacity loss off the state-of-charge records, holds out and bootstraps, and schedules the depot's night under the filed supply. It carries the pilot's fit to the thirty-nine blocks no electric bus has run on their kilometres, climb and speed, and extrapolates the pilot's flattened cold response to the design day, so every hard block's energy comes out 25 to 60 kWh light, more blocks clear the limit and more fit the night, and it orders about six buses too many; it dismisses the fuel-card file for the forecast because diesel litres do not measure battery energy, which is where the blocks' difficulty and the pilot heaters' share both sit.
domain_test: The results are a forecast carried from a selected sample to the population it was drawn from, where the selection was made on the outcome's own determinant as the old technology recorded it (the planner put the pilot on the blocks with the lowest diesel use), so the pilot's covariates cannot identify the between-block effect and the old technology's consumption record is the measurement of it; beside it, a measurement gap in the pilot's own record (heat the pilot took from fuel that the new buses take from the battery) read from a second record, a degradation share from state-of-charge logs, and a capacity constraint summed over the forecasts. With wards and nurses in place of blocks and buses there is no fuel record, no fuel-fired heater and no overnight charging supply; the count stops making sense.

driver: The decisive quantity is a count over many units of a per-unit forecast held against a limit and a shared nightly supply, where the units the forecast was fitted on were chosen for being the cheapest on the old technology, so the fit's covariates miss the difficulty the chooser selected on; that difficulty survives only in the old technology's consumption record, which the forecast's own data never mention and a solver dismisses as not measuring the new quantity, and the old units also took part of a load from a second energy source the new units take from the first; each unit's shortfall is small, the shortfalls all point one way, and the count comes out several units over.
driver_concrete: Each of Niittylä's 48 weekday blocks needs its battery energy on the standard's -15 C design day for the all-electric 2027 buses; the six pilot buses ran the nine blocks the planner picked from the 2024 fuel figures among the short blocks (46.2 against 49.1 l/100 km for the rest), so a model carried on kilometres, climb and hours per km under-forecasts the stop-heavy blocks, which the blocks' diesel use (tank to tank from the fuel-card statement over the dispatch log) carries at 0.031 kWh per km per l/100 km; the pilot buses' fuel-fired heaters supplied about 4.3 kW of cabin heat at -15 C that the quoted all-electric buses take from the battery (0.48 l/h of HVO from the statement's fills at the register's 35 kW for 3.9 l/h); every bus on charge draws through its charger beside the recharge about 3.5 kW on a -15 C night to keep its battery warm (0.46 kW plus 0.150 kW a degree below 5 C over the released hours, split from the sessions' metered energy, which the pooled ratio of 0.920 averages over mild nights), so the 690 kW night recharges 17 of the 23 qualifying blocks in the plan's priority order
stump: The careful pass (graded up: the heaters read from the HVO fills) carries the pilot's fit on kilometres, climb and hours per km, forecasts the hard blocks about 33 kWh light, passes 29 blocks, charges the night at the sessions' pooled ratio (0.920) and orders 18 under the night's capacity (29 without it); the pilot's cold-day consumption times kilometres orders 33; the diesel bridge put right alone orders 18, the conditioning alone 17 of another set, the heaters' share left out 19; the verdicts summed order 23, the night on battery energy 19
deep_chain: (1) each block's diesel use tank to tank; (2) the pilot blocks' gap to the rest; (3) the heat the pilot's fuel heaters supplied on the design day; (4) the 48 design-day energies through the diesel bridge; (5) the first-winter loss; (6) the verdicts; (7) what a bus on charge draws beside its recharge on a -15 C night, split from the charger meters; (8) the night's draw with every qualifying block on charge; (9) the count and the set.
judgment: a forecast fitted on a sample selected on the outcome's own determinant, identified through the old technology's record; a load the pilot took from fuel; a metered total split into its causes with the cold part carried to the design night; a capacity constraint over the forecasts
one_fact_test: the strongest sentence (the pilot blocks were chosen for their low diesel use, and the diesel figures carry what the covariates miss) rescues the selection, the energies and the verdicts and no conditioning, night or count: 3 of 9; the conditioning's sentence rescues 1

differentiation.task4: Architectures 5 to 9 forecast tractor duties from a pilot whose payloads were declared with error, a battery loss and a winter speed; every estimate was a per-unit mechanism a plot or a join showed and both runs landed it. Architecture 10 is a new world: the selection of the pilot's units on the old technology's own record, carried through a file the runs dismiss, accumulating over 48 units into a count under a shared supply; no declared weight, no calibration line, no speed ratio.
differentiation.mark132: mark132 sums a wear-out rate over positions whose failed items restart the curve; here nothing restarts: the forecast is carried from selected units to unselected ones through the old technology's consumption, and the count is capped by a shared nightly supply.
differentiation.mark124: mark124 reads a rate off units examined because they showed the outcome; here the units were selected on the determinant of the outcome by the planner, and the correction is a bridge through a second technology's record rather than the exhaustively examined groups' own rate.
differentiation.task12: task12 fades each entrant's response to a floor set by its pre-entry kind; here the selected units do not fade, they were simply the easiest, and the correction is the old technology's record of every unit.
differentiation.mark175: mark175 carries a take-up rate measured where access arrived first, to places whose runs are less taken; here nothing is a take-up or a run: the pilot's units were chosen on the old technology's own consumption record, the correction is a bridge through that record to units the pilot never ran, and the count is capped by a shared night supply.
differentiation.task7: task7 v7 instruments a lottery's passed-over arm; here there is no lottery and no arm: the pilot's blocks were picked on their diesel figures, and the diesel record of every block is the correction.
differentiation.task9: task9 v3 costs simulated storms at what a mutual's own claims show for storms like them; here nothing is simulated or a tail: a pilot's selected units are bridged to the unselected ones through the old technology's consumption record, and a count is capped by a night supply.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what handing a set of members of shared sequences to an outside provider saves, the time the sequences would no longer take: a member the sequence passes through on its way to others saves only its own stops beyond the direct run between its neighbours, and on a branch the near member saves the branch only when the members beyond it go too, so pricing each member at the time its own stops and the run into them take credits passed-through members with travel the sequences still make and, member by member, keeps the near member of a branch.
